Rashi on Chullin 81a:10:1.english: The second is unfit and [one is] exempt - because it is not accepted inside [the Temple courtyard]:

Rashi on Chullin 81a:10:2.hebrew: שני בלא תעשה - ולא בכרת, דלאו מתקבל בפנים הוא, דהא קמא שחיטה ראויה הואי:
Rashi on Chullin 81a:10:2.english: [For the] second [one, he is liable] for a negative commandment - And not for karet [excision], because it is not acceptable inside [the Temple], since the first [animal's slaughter] was a valid slaughter.

Rashi on Chullin 81a:13:1.hebrew: התראת ספק - דלמא לא אתי לידי זריקה, והויא ליה שחיטה שאינה ראויה, הלכך לר' שמעון איסורא איכא, מלקות ליכא; ומ"מ לאו מתקבל בפנים הוא, שהראשון שנשחט ונזרק הדם כבר קודם שחיטתו של שני, שחיטה ראויה הוה — כך שמעתי. וקשיא לי: מאי "התראת ספק" דקאמר? הא ודאי שחיטת שני אינה ראויה! דכיון דאיסור אותו ואת בנו נוהג בקדשים, הוה ליה שני מחוסר זמן, ואין שחיטתו ראויה, ואין כאן התראה כלל. ונראה בעיני דלא גרסינן ליה להאי "מ"ט", אלא: "אין מלקות אותו ואת בנו נוהג בקדשים", ותו לא מידי; וטעמא, משום דאין שחיטת השני ראויה — מכיון שנשחט ראשון ונזרק דמו, הויא לה שחיטת הראשון ראויה, דלית לן הא דלעיל דר' אושעיא, ודשני אינה ראויה, דהויא ליה מחוסר זמן ואין דמו נזרק. ופי' משובש הוא מאדם חריף ומפולפל:
Rashi on Chullin 81a:13:1.english: An uncertain forewarning - Perhaps it will not come to [the] sprinkling [of the blood], and it will be [considered] an unfit slaughter; therefore, according to Rabbi Shimon, there is a prohibition, [but] there are no lashes; and nevertheless, it is not [a case of] "accepted inside" [rendering the first slaughter unfit], since the first [animal], which was slaughtered and [whose] blood was already sprinkled prior to the slaughter of the second, was a fit slaughter — thus I have heard. But I have a difficulty [with this]: What is [this] "uncertain forewarning" that it speaks of? Surely the slaughter of the second [animal] is definitely unfit! For since the prohibition of "itself and its offspring" applies to consecrated [animals], the second [animal] is [considered] premature, so its slaughter is not fit, and there is no [valid] forewarning here at all. And it appears to me that we do not read this "What is the reason" [in the Gemara text], rather [it reads]: "lashes for [violating] itself and its offspring do not apply to consecrated [animals]," and nothing more; and the reason is because the slaughter of the second [animal] is not fit — once the first was slaughtered and its blood was sprinkled, the slaughter of the first is [deemed] fit, as we do not hold that [statement] above of Rabbi Oshaya, whereas that of the second is not fit, since it is premature and its blood is not sprinkled. And it is a corrupt explanation from a sharp and subtle person:

Rashi on Chullin 81a:14:1.english: And Rava follows his [own] reasoning - for he says [that] the slaughtering of "itself and its offspring" is an uncertain warning.

Rashi on Chullin 81a:14:2.hebrew: ואח"כ שחט שלמים - בו ביום:
Rashi on Chullin 81a:14:2.english: And afterward he slaughtered a peace offering - on that same day:

Rashi on Chullin 81a:14:3.hebrew: פטור - דהתראת ספק הוא, ואליבא דר' שמעון נקט מילתיה:
Rashi on Chullin 81a:14:3.english: [He is] exempt - For it is an uncertain forewarning, and [Rava] stated his ruling in accordance with Rabbi Shimon:

Rashi on Chullin 81a:15:1.hebrew: שלמים - בפנים, ואח"כ חולין בחוץ:
Rashi on Chullin 81a:15:1.english: A peace offering - [slaughtered] inside [the Temple courtyard], and afterward non-sacred [slaughtered] outside:

Rashi on Chullin 81a:15:2.hebrew: חייב - דהתראת ודאי היא, שכבר נזרק דמו של ראשון, והשני אינו מחוסר זריקה:
Rashi on Chullin 81a:15:2.english: Liable - for it is a definite forewarning, since the blood of the first [animal] has already been sprinkled, and the second [animal] does not require sprinkling:

Rashi on Chullin 81a:1:1.hebrew: נתקו לעשה - דמשמע בתוך זמנו ב"לא ירצה", כדמרבינן (תמורה דף ז: ע"ש) מ"ולנדר לא ירצה", אלא הניחו לאחר זמנו וירצה; דעל כרחך עשה זה לאו מעיקרא משמע, כי ההיא דשלוח הקן דאמרינן (לקמן חולין דף קמא.): מעיקרא משמע "שלח האם" ולא תקחנה, ולא הוי לאו הניתק לעשה ולוקין עליו; אבל כאן הלאו קודם לעשה, שהלאו בתוך זמנו והעשה לאחר זמנו:
Rashi on Chullin 81a:1:1.english: Transmuted it into a positive mitzva - For [an offering] within its [prohibited] time is subject to [the prohibition of] "it shall not be accepted," as we derive (Temurah 7b, see there) from [the verse] "and for a vow it shall not be accepted"; rather, leave it until after its time [has passed], and it will be accepted. For perforce this positive mitzva does not apply initially [before the prohibition], like that [case] of sending away the mother bird, where we say (below, Chullin 141a) [that it] applies initially — "send away the mother" and do not take her — and [therefore] it is not a prohibition transmuted into a positive mitzva, and one receives lashes for [violating] it. But here, the prohibition precedes the positive mitzva, for the prohibition [applies] within its time and the positive mitzva [applies] after its time:

Rashi on Chullin 81a:2:1.hebrew: מיבעי ליה לכדר' אפטוריקי - ולאו לעשה אתא:
Rashi on Chullin 81a:2:1.english: It is required for [the statement] of Rabbi Aptoriki - and it does not come [to teach] a positive commandment:

Rashi on Chullin 81a:3:1.english: How so? The night - [i.e., the night of the] eighth [day], when the seventh [day] has passed:

Rashi on Chullin 81a:3:2.hebrew: לקדושה - מותר לקדשו משחשכה, ואינו עובר משום בל תקדיש פסולים:
Rashi on Chullin 81a:3:2.english: For consecration - it is permitted to consecrate it once it grows dark, and one does not transgress on account of [the prohibition], "Do not consecrate disqualified [animals]":

Rashi on Chullin 81a:5:1.hebrew: שני בלא תעשה - דשחוטי חוץ, ואע"פ שאינו בכרת, דלאו מתקבל בפנים הוא, מ"מ בלא תעשה הוא, הואיל ורצוי לאחר זמן. ולאו דידיה מפרש בפרק בתרא דזבחים (דף קיד.) מ"לא תעשון ככל אשר אנחנו עושים וגו'":
Rashi on Chullin 81a:5:1.english: The second [is subject] to a prohibition - of slaughtering [sacrifices] outside [the Temple]. Even though it does not [incur] karet [excision], since it is not [fit to be] accepted inside [the Temple], nevertheless it is [subject] to a prohibition, since it will be acceptable after [some] time. And its prohibition is explained in the last chapter of Zevachim (114a) from [the verse], "You shall not do according to all that we do, etc.":

Rashi on Chullin 81a:6:1.hebrew: קמא מקטל קטלה - לר' שמעון, דהא שחיטה שאינה ראויה היא:
Rashi on Chullin 81a:6:1.english: The first [animal], he [merely] killed it - according to Rabbi Shimon, since it is an unfit slaughter:

Rashi on Chullin 81a:7:1.english: And Rava said - This is the reading [we have]:

Rashi on Chullin 81a:7:2.english: According to the Rabbis - who say [that] an unfit slaughter is considered slaughter:

Rashi on Chullin 81a:7:3.hebrew: שני פסול ופטור - מכרת, דלא מתקבל בפנים הוא:
Rashi on Chullin 81a:7:3.english: The second [animal] is disqualified and [one is] exempt - from karet, because it is not acceptable inside [the Temple]:

Rashi on Chullin 81a:8:1.hebrew: לרבי שמעון שניהם ענושין כרת - קמא מקטל קטליה, ושני מתקבל בפנים הוא; ולענין שחוטי חוץ, אף על גב דאינה ראויה מיחייב, דאפילו אהך שחיטה חייביה רחמנא:
Rashi on Chullin 81a:8:1.english: According to Rabbi Shimon, both of them are punishable by karet - The first one he merely killed [i.e., its slaughter is not legally considered a valid slaughter], and [therefore] the second one is [fit to be] accepted inside [the Temple]. And regarding [the prohibition of] slaughtering outside [the Temple], even though it is an unfit [slaughter], he is liable, for the Merciful One obligated him even for this [kind of] slaughter:

Rashi on Chullin 81a:9:1.hebrew: אחד בחוץ - תחלה, ואח"כ אחד בפנים:
Rashi on Chullin 81a:9:1.english: One outside - first, and afterwards one inside:

Rashi on Chullin 81a:9:2.hebrew: שני פסול ופטור - מכרת. ובלאו ד"אותו ואת בנו" לא מיירי התם, דגבי שחוטי חוץ קאי. והא "פטור" לא איצטריך, אלא איידי דתני "ראשון חייב", תנא "שני פטור":
Rashi on Chullin 81a:9:2.english: The second is disqualified and [he is] exempt - from karet. And regarding the negative prohibition of "it and its offspring," it is not dealing [with that] there, as it is addressing [the laws of] animals slaughtered outside [the Temple]. And this [statement that he is] "exempt" was not necessary; rather, since it taught "the first is liable," it [also] taught "the second is exempt":

Rashi on Chullin 81a:9:3.hebrew: לר' שמעון שני כשר - דקמא מיקטל קטליה, ושני לאו מחוסר זמן הוא. כל הנך פטורי דהכא משחוטי חוץ קאמר, ולא איירי בלאו דאותו ואת בנו כלל:
Rashi on Chullin 81a:9:3.english: According to Rabbi Shimon, the second is fit - Because he merely killed the first one [i.e., it is not legally considered slaughter], and [thus] the second is not [disqualified as] premature. All these [rulings of] "exempt" [mentioned] here are stated regarding [the liability for] slaughtering outside [the Temple courtyard], and [the Gemara] is not addressing the prohibition of "itself and its offspring" at all:

Tosafot on Chullin 81a:3:1.hebrew: יום להרצאה - וא"ת: מ"ביום צוותו" נפקא (מגילה דף כ:) "ביום ולא בלילה"! וי"ל: דמההוא קרא לא הוה פסלינן לילה שאחר שבעה אלא כמו שאר לילות, ואם עלה לא ירד; להכי צריך קרא דהכא, דהוי מחוסר זמן ואם עלה ירד. ותימה, דר"ש הוא דאית ליה ב"המזבח מקדש" (זבחים פד.), ואי רבי אפטוריקי כר"ש, מאי פריך מיניה? דסוגיא דהכא, דפריך "ולילקי נמי משום מחוסר זמן", לא פריך אלא לרבנן; דלר' שמעון הכי נמי דלקי, כדאמר בפ' בתרא דזבחים (דף קיד:)! ושמא ר' זירא דהכא סבר ליה כרב נחמן בר יצחק, דאמר התם דלר' שמעון נמי לא לקי. ועוד י"ל: דנפקא מיניה הא דפסול משום מחוסר זמן, דפסול אף בבמה, אבל פסול לילה ליכא בבמה לשמואל בשילהי זבחים (דף קכ.):
Tosafot on Chullin 81a:3:1.english: Day for effecting acceptance - And if you will say: Is it not derived from "on the day He commanded" (Megillah 20b): "By day, and not by night"? And one can answer: From that verse we would only disqualify the night after the seventh [day] like other nights, [where] if it went up [on the altar] it does not come down; therefore, the verse here is needed, [to teach] that it is premature [mechusar zeman], and if it went up it must come down. And [this is] astonishing! For it is Rabbi Shimon who holds [this] in [the chapter] HaMizbe'ach Mekadesh (Zevachim 84a); and if Rabbi Aftoriki [holds] like Rabbi Shimon, how does [the Gemara] raise an objection from him? For the sugya here, which asks, "And let him also incur lashes on account of premature [time]," only asks according to the Rabbis; for according to Rabbi Shimon, indeed he does incur lashes, as it says in the last chapter of Zevachim (114b)! And perhaps Rabbi Zeira here holds like Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak, who says there that according to Rabbi Shimon as well, he does not incur lashes. And furthermore, one can say: What emerges from the fact that it is disqualified on account of premature [time] is that it is disqualified even on a high place [bama], whereas disqualification by night does not apply on a high place according to Shmuel at the end of Zevachim (120a):
